classification.difficultyReason: Find zeros, determine signs between successive zeros and combine intercepts with end behaviour to sketch quadratic and cubic curves.

content.prompt: Identify the zeros of each polynomial. Draw sign diagrams and sketch the curves.

answer.short: Zeros: $x=2,4$. Signs from left to right: $+,0,-,0,+$. The upward-opening parabola passes through $(0,8)$ and crosses the $x$-axis at both zeros.
answer.worked:
Setting each factor equal to zero gives $x=2$ or $x=4$.

Test one point in each interval:
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=(-2)(-4)=8>0\\y(3)&=(1)(-1)=-1<0\\y(5)&=(3)(1)=3>0.\end{align*}$$
The sign diagram is positive for $x<2$, negative for $2<x<4$ and positive for $x>4$, with zero at both boundaries. The $y$-intercept is $(0,8)$. Draw a smooth upward-opening parabola crossing at $(2,0)$ and $(4,0)$.

spec.description: Complete sign diagram and equation-derived parabola, with both zeros and the y-intercept labelled.

answer.short: Zeros: $x=0,2,4$. Signs from left to right: $-,0,+,0,-,0,+$. The cubic crosses at every zero, descending to the left and rising to the right.
answer.worked:
Setting each factor equal to zero gives $x=0,2,4$.

Test one point in each interval:
$$\begin{align*}y(-1)&=(-1)(-3)(-5)=-15<0\\y(1)&=(1)(-1)(-3)=3>0\\y(3)&=(3)(1)(-1)=-3<0\\y(5)&=(5)(3)(1)=15>0.\end{align*}$$
The signs alternate $-,+,-,+$. The graph crosses the $x$-axis at all three zeros and passes through the origin. Its leading term is $x^3$, so the left end descends and the right end rises. Join the intercepts with a smooth cubic consistent with the sign diagram.

spec.description: Complete sign diagram and equation-derived cubic crossing all three marked zeros.
spec.mathematics: Zeros 0,2,4; signs -,+,-,+; positive cubic leading coefficient.

answer.short: Zeros: $x=-3,1,3$. Signs from left to right: $-,0,+,0,-,0,+$. The cubic crosses at every zero and passes through $(0,9)$.
answer.worked:
Setting each factor equal to zero gives $x=-3,1,3$.

Test one point in each interval:
$$\begin{align*}y(-4)&=(-1)(-5)(-7)=-35<0\\y(0)&=(3)(-1)(-3)=9>0\\y(2)&=(5)(1)(-1)=-5<0\\y(4)&=(7)(3)(1)=21>0.\end{align*}$$
The signs alternate $-,+,-,+$. Plot the three zeros and the $y$-intercept $(0,9)$. The leading term is $x^3$, so the left end descends and the right end rises. Draw a smooth cubic crossing at each zero and lying on the side of the axis indicated by the sign diagram.

spec.description: Complete sign diagram and equation-derived cubic, with three zeros and y-intercept labelled.

answer.short: Zeros: $x=-2,-1,3$. Signs from left to right: $-,0,+,0,-,0,+$. The cubic crosses at every zero and passes through $(0,-6)$.
answer.worked:
Setting each factor equal to zero gives $x=-2,-1,3$.

Test one point in each interval:
$$\begin{align*}y(-3)&=(-1)(-2)(-6)=-12<0\\y\left(-\frac32\right)&=\left(\frac12\right)\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac92\right)=\frac98>0\\y(0)&=(2)(1)(-3)=-6<0\\y(4)&=(6)(5)(1)=30>0.\end{align*}$$
The signs alternate $-,+,-,+$. Plot the three zeros and the $y$-intercept $(0,-6)$. The leading term is $x^3$, so the left end descends and the right end rises. Draw a smooth cubic crossing at each zero and lying on the side of the axis indicated by the sign diagram.
